name: navigator.plugins and mimeTypes
plain: List of browser plugins and MIME types; now a fixed list of 5 PDF viewers.
meaning: Once the strongest fingerprint (15.4 bits, Flash and Java era). Since Chrome 94 and Firefox 99 it returns a hardcoded PDF list, so it now mostly flags headless or odd browsers.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: plugins
fields.range: 5 entries: PDF Viewer, Chrome PDF Viewer, Chromium PDF Viewer, Microsoft Edge PDF Viewer, WebKit built-in PDF

limits.headline: Can see a fixed list of 5 PDF viewers, so it no longer tells you apart
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Get the same hard coded list of PDF viewers
Spot a headless or odd browser when the list looks wrong
Check it with other signs of automation
cannot: See real plugins; Chrome 94 and Firefox 99 stopped listing them
Tell regular visitors apart; the list is the same
See which Flash or Java version you have; those plugins are gone

story.what_it_is: The list of browser plugins, now a fixed list of five PDF viewers in modern browsers.

marketing.name: Navigator.plugins
marketing.pitch: Docs say the list is now a fixed set for PDF viewing, kept only for compatibility.

story.for_you: You never see it. It used to list tools like Flash and Java, which made people very easy to tell apart. Now every browser says the same five PDF viewers, so it hardly tells anything.
story.for_makers: In the Flash era this was one of the strongest fingerprints. Now sites mostly use it to spot automation, because a headless browser often gives an empty or odd list. It also shows that a browser is being faked.

use_cases.example: A bot defence service flags a visitor with zero plugins as probably headless.
An ad fraud vendor discards ad views from clients with empty plugin lists.
A browser games portal blocks automated clients farming rewards when the plugin list looks fake.
A ticket seller adds a missing plugin list to its bot score during a high demand sale.
A traffic report removes visits that look like headless tools.
An old site still reads the list to choose a PDF viewer, which now always works.

linkedin.how: Collected as plugins and MIME types. Read by the LinkedIn APFC fingerprint script (48 features, alleged by BrowserGate, partly confirmed by BleepingComputer).

history.change: Panopticlick measures plugins list at 15.4 bits
Flash plugins end of life; NPAPI gone since Chrome 45
Plugins and mimeTypes return fixed PDF entries when PDF viewer enabled
